sources.title: Spiritual Machines: The Merging of Man and Machine — Ray Kurzweil

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Typical adult workers spend a majority of their time acquiring new knowledge/skills as a primary activity, not merely incidental learning while doing any job.
reference.rationale: BLS time-use evidence does not resemble a majority of time devoted to study/retraining. Continuing education remains important, but calling all productive work “learning” would make the forecast untestable. On an ordinary primary-activity reading it remains a miss.

evidence.title: BLS: Time use of millennials and nonmillennials
evidence.note: Time-use study separates work and educational activity. Does not fully count informal on-the-job learning, which is an interpretation limitation.. broader.criterion: Knowledge acquisition and recurrent retraining become important parts of working life.
broader.rationale: This qualitative lifelong-learning direction is plausible and widely consistent with digital work, but lacks a global majority-time claim.
